To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the verification of a data-insensitive circuit can be reduced to the verification of an abstract sequential circuit (2) the verification of an in-order-retirement out-of-order execution circuit can be reduced (deductively) to the verification of a sequential instruction execution circuit.

(1) we present a new verification algorithm, (2) we prove that it is correct by proving that it refines a known correct algorithm, and (3) we use the refinement to show the correctness of the new algorithm.
1. We present an algorithm for out of order execution with in-order-retirement and show it to refine sequential execution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an abstract model for the verification of data-insensitive circuits.
the following question: How can one use deductive methods to establish the refinement of a complex system with respect to a simpler system?
the development of efficient algorithms for verification of data-insensitive circuits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the out-of-order circuit is correct if and only if the sequential circuit is correct.
the verification of out-of-order execution circuits with in-order retirement can be reduced to the verification of sequential execution circuits.
the out-of-order execution algorithm is a refinement of the sequentially executing instruction execution algorithm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the verification of the out-of- order algorithm with in-order retirement is as hard as the verification of the sequential algorithm.
we have developed a model and algorithm for out-of order execution with in-order retirements and verified it using pvs.
we have developed a new model for data-insensitive circuits and have used it to verify an important out-of-order execution component.

the use of unifying models for data-insensitive circuits can lead to a better understanding of the underlying circuit structure and can help in the development of efficient algorithms for verification of such circuits.
